extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of philosophy (and writers interested in philosophical accounts of mind, language, life, and representation)
extracted.subtask_description: Philosophical guidance for representing life, movement, instinct, and language in writing — how intellect and instinct differently apprehend continuity, novelty, and form, and implications for depiction. Useful for creative writers aiming to portray lived continuity versus discrete, objectified states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Of the discontinuous alone does the intellect form a clear idea
rubrics_metrics.description: "Of the discontinuous alone does the intellect form a clear idea."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The intellect prefers discontinuity and treats reality by choosing modes of decomposition (immobile units) that make action possible. For representation, this is a warning that intellectual modes naturally break continuity into discrete, manipulable 'units' — a useful practical method but one that risks misrepresenting living continuity. Antipattern: assuming that the only legitimate or "clear" way to present phenomena is as separate, stable parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Of immobility alone does the intellect form a clear idea
rubrics_metrics.description: "Of immobility alone does the intellect form a clear idea."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intellect starts from immobility and constructs movement by assembling immobile states; this tendency serves practical fabrication but is philosophically illegitimate for grasping true mobility. For writers: relying solely on static snapshots or fixed states to convey movement or becoming will miss the living flux; consider techniques that foreground process and continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellect's unlimited power to decompose and recompose matter
rubrics_metrics.description: "The intellect is characterized by the unlimited power of decomposing according to any law and of recomposing into any system."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intelligence treats matter as indifferent, a medium to be carved and remade (a homogeneous space projected behind extension). In creative practice this explains a tendency to treat characters, bodies, or situations as materials for manipulation — effective for 'fabrication' but prone to objectifying living complexity. Use this as a criterion: does the work merely recompose fixed parts, or does it respect organic interpenetration?

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobility of the sign (language) vs adherent instinctive sign
rubrics_metrics.description: "The instinctive sign is adherent, the intelligent sign is mobile."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Human language's signs can transfer from object to object and from thing to idea; this mobility allowed reflection and the discovery of an internal world. For writers: exploit the 'mobility' of words (metaphor, metonymy, shifting reference) to move from concrete perception into inner life. Antipattern: assuming words must remain rigidly tied to a single referent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language converts processes into objects — facilitation and danger
rubrics_metrics.description: Language makes an object of the word (external and immaterial), and by 'covering up' an object converts it into a thing; thus the word allows the intellect to penetrate its own workings but also tends to objectify what it names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using language to make inner life visible is powerful, yet naming risks freezing flux into objectified concepts. For creative writers: be aware that naming clarifies but can also deaden; choose forms that preserve movement (e.g., verbs, progressive aspect, or associative imagery) when you want to keep life fluid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellect's natural inability to comprehend life
rubrics_metrics.description: "The intellect is characterized by a natural inability to comprehend life."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the intellect seeks given, stable elements and calculable causality, it cannot truly think pure mobility, novelty, or the unforeseeable upspringing of the new. As an evaluative criterion: examine whether a portrayal of living processes forces them into pre-given categories and linear causality, thereby losing the sense of emergence and novelty that characterizes life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellect represents becoming as a series of homogeneous states
rubrics_metrics.description: The intellect 'represents becoming as a series of states, each of which is homogeneous with itself and consequently does not change.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exposes a common representational move: to render change by stitching together static states. For narrative technique, ask whether the sequence of scenes truly conveys internal transformation or merely substitutes static equivalents. Antipattern: infinite subdivision into ever-smaller immutable states to 'explain' change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intelligence substitutes practical equivalents for movement
rubrics_metrics.description: When intelligence substitutes for movement immobilities put together, it does not pretend to reconstitute the movement such as it actually is; it merely replaces it with a practical equivalent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that practical/story logic may intentionally simplify ﬂux for intelligibility. As a criterion, decide whether such simplification serves the work's aims or flattens lifelike complexity. Use tactics (stream-of-consciousness, durational scenes, sensory continuity) when reconstituting lived movement is desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instinct is organic knowledge molded on life
rubrics_metrics.description: "Instinct ... is molded on the very form of life. While intelligence treats everything mechanically, instinct proceeds, so to speak, organically."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instinct operates as an internal, non-analytical knowledge (e.g., bees, cells, wasps show complex, integrated behaviors). For character or natural description, treat instinctual actions as unified, integrated wholes rather than as composite learned bits. Antipattern: explaining instinctive behavior purely in terms of external, segmented causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science translates instinct into intelligence but can only imitate it
rubrics_metrics.description: Science 'constructs an imitation of instinct rather than penetrates within it' by translating instinct into intelligent/mechanistic terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid reducing instinctive or organic phenomena in fiction to mere mechanistic explanations if you want to preserve their lived mystery. As an evaluative standard: does the portrayal acknowledge the limits of analytic translation and preserve a sense of irreducible immediacy?

rubrics_metrics.name: Instincts evolve as whole themes with variations, not mere accretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Instinct is 'everywhere complete, but ... more or less simplified, and, above all, simplified differently.' Evolution of instinct often looks like variations on a theme rather than successive additive steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When imagining developmental or evolutionary change (species, cultures, psychologies), consider forms of variation that transform an entire pattern rather than append isolated new parts. For worldbuilding and characterization, prefer holistic variations and patterned transpositions over simple additive 'progress.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual explanation tends to reconstitute the new from the old
rubrics_metrics.description: Explaining invention or the 'upspringing' of the new always consists, for the intellect, in resolving it into elements old or known, arranged in a different order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a criterion for originality in creative work: beware of explanations that retroject novelty as merely recombination of earlier elements. If the work claims to capture genuine emergence, craft techniques that let the new appear irreducible (unexpected associations, moments of affective surprise, stylistic breaks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of language enables reflection and discovery of inner workings
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the word is external yet immaterial and mobile, 'the intelligence can penetrate even to the inwardness of its own work' and discover a whole internal world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage this property: use the mobility of words to move between sensory detail, memory, image, and metacognition, thereby rendering consciousness and reflection. But remain aware that this process also tends to objectify; balance naming with dynamic forms to preserve subjectivity.
